messages.subject: Different interval for scales
parts:
Hi @all

After hours of trying (again) I gave up and hope that someone in this
forum might be able to help me with the following problem. I have a
plot where the y-axis interval is 5. However, when I delete the
scale_y limits, the interval between my y-axis values is 2. How can I
control the interval of my y-axis when I use the scale_y limit call? I
don't mean the break call as this only adds additional breaks in
between the y-axis ticks. Any idea?


read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/4236038/dotplots_all.csv") ->
nutrients
p<-ggplot(nutrients, aes(x = d18O, y = dD, shape=factor(Water)))
p+geom_point()
p<-ggplot(nutrients, aes(x = d18O, y = dD, shape=factor(Water),
color=factor(Catchment)))
p+geom_point(size=4)+ geom_abline(intercept = 10.8, slope = 8.13)
+geom_abline(intercept = 12.56, slope = 7.72, linetype="dashed")+
theme_bw() + opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill=NULL,colour=NULL)) +
opts(legend.position = "bottom") +
xlab(expression(paste(delta^{18},'O'~'(\u2030)'))) +
ylab(expression(paste(delta,'D'~'(\u2030)'))) + opts(axis.text.x =
theme_text(size=13), axis.text.y = theme_text(size=13, hjust = 0.8),
legend.title = theme_text(size=15), legend.text =
theme_text(size=15),
axis.title.x = theme_text(size=15), axis.title.y =
theme_text(size=15,
angle = 90)) + opts(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.4))+
opts(legend.background=theme_rect(col = "black")) +
opts(panel.border
= theme_rect(colour = 'black')) + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-5,2))
+
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-20,15))

messages.subject: Re: Different interval for scales
parts:
This gives my the y scale with an interval of 5. However, I would like
to have an interval of 2, but not in the sense of just showing a tick
mark every 2 intervals. When I use my code without the scale_x_cont
and scale_y_cont limits I get a plot where the y-axis ticks show
-6,-8-,10 etc. However, when I use the code with the limits then I
will get values of -5,-10,-15 but with the same distance between each
tick compared to the the plot without the limits set. I would like to
maintain the same visual spread of data with the new limits set. When
I just add manual breaks then the visual data spread stays the same
and only the tick marks are added. I hope that does not sound too
confusing.

This code shows the graph without the limits set, hence the interval
of the y-axis is 2:

nutrients$col<-paste(nutrients$Water, nutrients$Catchment) #merge by
paste
p<-ggplot(nutrients, aes(x = d18O, y = dD, shape=factor(col)))
p+geom_point(size=3)+ geom_abline(intercept = 10.8, slope = 8.13)

+geom_abline(intercept = 12.56, slope = 7.72, linetype="dashed")+
theme_bw() + opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill=NULL,colour=NULL)) +
opts(legend.position = "bottom") +
xlab(expression(paste(delta^{18},'O'~'(\u2030)'))) +
ylab(expression(paste(delta,'D'~'(\u2030)'))) + opts(axis.text.x =
theme_text(size=13), axis.text.y = theme_text(size=13, hjust = 0.8),
legend.title = theme_text(size=15), legend.text = theme_text(size=15),
axis.title.x = theme_text(size=15), axis.title.y = theme_text(size=15,
angle = 90)) + opts(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.4))+

This code sets the limits and suddenly the same distance used for each
interval on the y-axis is used but the new interval is 5. That lets
the data shrink visually. I would like to maintain the same space
between each tick mark and have an interval of 2 (like in the first
plot) but with the new limits that will increase the y-axis range:

nutrients$col<-paste(nutrients$Water, nutrients$Catchment) #merge by
paste
p<-ggplot(nutrients, aes(x = d18O, y = dD, shape=factor(col)))
p+geom_point(size=3)+ geom_abline(intercept = 10.8, slope = 8.13)

+geom_abline(intercept = 12.56, slope = 7.72, linetype="dashed")+
theme_bw() + opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill=NULL,colour=NULL)) +
opts(legend.position = "bottom") +
xlab(expression(paste(delta^{18},'O'~'(\u2030)'))) +
ylab(expression(paste(delta,'D'~'(\u2030)'))) + opts(axis.text.x =
theme_text(size=13), axis.text.y = theme_text(size=13, hjust = 0.8),
legend.title = theme_text(size=15), legend.text = theme_text(size=15),
axis.title.x = theme_text(size=15), axis.title.y = theme_text(size=15,
angle = 90)) + opts(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.4))+
